rule: capital and risk are the owner's own facts: he declared the capital and delegated the risk policy to the Architect on 2026-09-30, and on 2026-10-01 asked that size follow the quality of the setup rather than be restricted by default. An object graded strong is sized at risk_pct_strong, one graded medium at risk_pct_medium, and either is multiplied by risk_mult_high where the exceptional-risk label prints (ANALYST-INSTRUCTIONS.md sections 2, 4 and 8). The capital changes only on his declaration of his account size; the policy changes only by an owner decision or at the scorecard gate of SYSTEM-MAP-CRYPTOCALCUL.md section 10. The engine reads this file and never writes it. A vectors entry is a hypothesis with no authority: it is resolved against a primary source or reported unresolved with the host that was read. Since v4 (2026-11-18) the card block sizes every card of the analysis answer by the owner's decisions of that day: a margin by rank between margin_min_usdt and margin_max_usdt, the larger margin for the stronger card, the leverage the rank's risk allows on it and never one at which the stop fills after liquidation, up to his own lev_max of 15 (ANALYST-INSTRUCTIONS.md sections 2, 4 and 8). Since v5 (2026-11-21, the owner's own rule) the leverage never falls under lev_min of 3, and portfolio_max_pct left with the portfolio line he struck out. The risk block keeps sizing the scorecard and the paper test unchanged, so their records do not restart; risk_mult_high halves a card's risk where the exceptional-risk label prints.

vectors.claim: Large holders are accumulating UNI. No source, no figures. Resolve against a primary only: an on-chain flow with a named address, or an exchange or foundation report. A repeat across aggregators is not a quorum. Note that UNI already sits in AVOID for a structural reason - a high-beta name at the top of its range in risk-off - which is a statement about entry timing and does not contradict this claim; both can hold at once, and the run must not read one as refuting the other. Carried unresolved since it was raised: every run reports it with the host it read, or reports that it did not work on it. 'Not acted on' is not one of its three states.
